summary:
Nusfaire – One true fire record, for any country on Earth

When NASA satellites look at Oman, they see nearly half a million hot spots, but most of them are not fires. Almost 9 out of 10 are gas flares and industrial heat from oil, gas and factories. The record is also split: NASA’s older MODIS sensor has watched since 2000, while the newer VIIRS, active since 2012, sees about nine times more. Put the two together and fires seem to grow every year, even when nothing has changed.

Nusfaire fixes this. Our web app removes flares and industrial heat, then puts both satellites on one scale, month by month, to create a single, reliable fire record from 2000 to today. We tested it by hiding MODIS data and rebuilding it from VIIRS alone, and the results closely matched the real data.

Users pick any area and period, see when fires really happen, spot unusual months, and download a ready PDF report. It was built and tested in Oman, but it works worldwide: any country can upload its own free NASA FIRMS data.

Next, we will link Nusfaire directly with civil defence, meteorology and environmental authorities, so they get alerts when fire activity becomes unusual.
details:
What it does and how it works
Nusfaire is a web app that turns two NASA fire records into one reliable fire history from 2000 to today. NASA has two fire sensors: MODIS (since 2000) and VIIRS (since 2012). VIIRS has sharper pixels, so it sees about nine times more hot spots. If you join the two records as they are, fires seem to jump suddenly in 2012, even though only the sensor changed.

Nusfaire fixes this in three steps. First, it removes hot spots that are not fires, such as gas flares and factories, using NASA’s own labels and places that stay hot all year. Second, it measures how many more hot spots VIIRS sees than MODIS for each month and each area, then converts both onto one scale. Third, it builds a burn calendar that shows when fires normally happen, which months are unusual, and how activity changes over the years.

Users choose any area and time period on a map. They can download the results as CSV files or as a ready PDF report.

Benefits and intended impact
In Oman, almost 9 out of 10 satellite hot spots come from oil, gas and industry, not fires. Without cleaning and harmonization, decision makers would see a false picture. Nusfaire gives civil defence, meteorology, environment and climate agencies, and researchers a clean, long-term fire record they can trust. The record helps them plan for fire seasons, spot unusual activity, and study long-term trends. It also protects 12 extra years of history as MODIS is retired, because we showed that VIIRS can continue the same record.

Tools and technologies

  • NASA FIRMS active fire data (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375 m: S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21)
  • Python and pandas for data preparation and validation
  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the web app, with no server needed
  • html2canvas and jsPDF for PDF reports
  • GitHub Pages for hosting
  • An AI assistant (Claude) helped with coding and writing; our team designed, tested and reviewed all of the work

Creativity
Most tools show raw hot spots. Nusfaire corrects the record first and then explains it in simple language. We tested our method in a creative way: we pretended MODIS had stopped, rebuilt its data from VIIRS alone, and compared the result with the real values. Simply switching sensors gave an error of about 820%. Our method cut that error to about 42%. The app supports English and Arabic, works on phones, and accepts any country’s FIRMS data.

Factors we considered

  • Different sensor resolutions and satellite overpass times
  • Seasonal changes in the gap between the sensors (larger in winter, smaller in summer)
  • Separating real fires from gas flares and industrial heat
  • Areas with very few fires, where numbers can be unstable
  • Easy use for non-experts, in Arabic and English
  • Free, open data, so any country can use it

Next step
We plan to link Nusfaire directly with civil defence and other authorities so they receive automatic alerts when fire activity becomes unusual.
